evidence:
Scope: direct manual review of the complete frozen instruction.md and all six participant-facing notes, using the actual XLSX via openpyxl. rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks row 3 (#2), says "Keeps an authentic human voice (casual/terse is good); not robotic, over-polished, or LLM-generated prose." Its Internal Quality Checks row 3 repeats that wording, with no additional populated annotation or cell comment. The bundled rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/assets/WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx has the same row and Internal interpretation. rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:13-15 calls for sentence variety, contractions and terse phrasing, and warns about uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets and voice changes. This is a voice assessment, not an assertion about authorship provenance.

Concrete evidence (all task citations are beneath .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task): instruction.md:1 opens "I'd like a small code playground for trying out browser ideas" and ends with the short "No accounts or sign-in; it's a local tool." instruction.md:3 gives the owner's reason, "The annoying part with playgrounds is losing something that was working," then describes an error/Stop recovery and a two-editor concern in ordinary language. instruction.md:5 says "There isn't a starter app to finish"; instruction.md:7 asks for a workspace that "should feel ready to use." These vary sentence length and structure rather than repeating a polished requirement formula.

Voice remains consistent across every note. environment/instructions/overview.md:3 says "When I open the app, I want useful code already there" and :5 says "I shouldn't have to keep a separate selector in sync." environment/instructions/ui.md:3 begins "I'd like the editor, preview and console visible as three useful panes"; :9 adds "I should be able to navigate without a pointer." environment/instructions/behaviour.md:9 uses the brief clarification "A timer doesn't get a new five seconds when it fires"; :13 says "I don't want half of the failed attempt left behind"; :21 says "About two seconds after I stop typing is plenty"; :29 explains conflicts as "Keep my unsaved work so I can compare it with the latest copy." The precise execution and revision semantics have an intelligible user reason and retain ordinary sentence variety. environment/instructions/security.md:5 says "This doesn't promise to interrupt arbitrary blocking browser-native operations or generated machine code" and :7 explains that the same words in strings/comments/HTML are harmless; the greater precision fits a security boundary rather than introducing marketing or robotic cadence. environment/instructions/policy.md:1 is "A few product choices" and :5 leaves choices to the builder in plain language. environment/instructions/integration.md:1 is "How we start the app"; :3 says the suggested frontend tools "would be convenient" but are "up to you"; :7 says "Starting again shouldn't duplicate examples or saved records." Its concrete deployment nouns are necessary operating details, not evidence of unnatural voice. The frozen template integration note likewise uses explicit runtime facts, so I did not invent a requirement to make such notes informal or remove the template contract. All seven files were read completely; no alternating owner/marketing voice, repeated ceremonial introductions, or perfectly parallel acceptance bullets were observed.

The seven task prose files, both inspected XLSX files, SKILL.md, all three reference documents and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md were independently SHA256-checked against manifest.json; all 14 checked entries matched. The manifest and raw-evidence-index.json bind input 27f81c18259555d26b61a5a2b0f026f0360b7380bc072523513b0ad2deca9efc. Current review policy was applied: no keyword count or contraction count substitutes for reading the whole request, and missing configured-judge/Oracle/target-model runs remain unmeasured. Those runs are not required to observe the wording for this row. No prior or peer verdicts were read and no task source was changed.
counterexample: Manual false-fail challenge: the actual conforming integration.md:5 passage, "Put the finished app and everything it needs to start in /app. We start it with node /app/server.js," contains exact paths and commands but retains a natural practical voice. A rule that rejects technical terms or imperative sentences would falsely fail it. The actual security.md:7 boundary list is similarly reasonable precision, not proof of robotic wording. Manual false-pass challenge: a hypothetical replacement could retain the current "I'd like" opener, then say "The system shall execute JavaScript. The system shall execute HTML. The system shall execute CSS. The system shall provide seamless, robust snippet management." A contraction/word-presence heuristic could accept that mutated request while its uniform cadence and gloss violate this row. Reading all seven current files distinguishes it; no such mutation is present. A broken app with a dead Run button and the unchanged current prose could still pass this voice row legitimately: implementation functionality belongs to other rows, so this Pass does not assert that a working app or successful judge run exists.
